CHEMISTRY — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti? (1 mark)

   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.

   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole.

11. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru? (1 mark)

14. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

16. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea? (1 mark)

   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.

19. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
